    Tech Report: CMS Market Share Trends: Top Content Management Systems (Nov 2026) via @sejournal, @theshelleywalsh

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that wordPress might remain the dominant force in content management systems (CMS) for now, but market share has dropped since its peak in 2022 to under 60%.
    • WordPress still remains a substantial lead over its nearest rival, Shopify, but is this an indication of a downturn for WordPress, or for the general usage of CMS?
    • Sources indicate that shopify has continued its growth across all surveyed websites, with Wix and Squarespace also maintaining their growth trajectory.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that wordPress might remain the dominant force in content management systems (CMS) for now, but market share has dropped since its peak in 2022 to under 60%. According to W3Techs on Nov. 13, 2026, WordPress now has a CMS market share of 57.9%. Looking at historical data, WordPress dipped under 60% in 2016, 2017, and 2019, but this is the lowest drop since 2013.

    WordPress still remains a substantial lead over its nearest rival, Shopify, but is this an indication of a downturn for WordPress, or for the general usage of CMS?

    Sources indicate that shopify has continued its growth across all surveyed websites, with Wix and Squarespace also maintaining their growth trajectory. In fact, apart from Joomla and Drupal, which fell, and Webflow, which held flat, all other top CMS have increased market share, indicating WordPress is on a downturn to the benefit of other platforms.

    This report breaks down the current CMS landscape, compares the top platforms, and outlines the latest shifts in market share and usage.

    According to W3Techs, 67.7% of websites have a CMS, and Netcraft reports over 323 million domains.

    From this, we can assume that the current market size for content management systems has risen to 218.8 million websites.

    *Approximations extrapolated from W3Techs and Netcraft data.

    There are two different measures throughout this report: usage is a platform’s percentage of all surveyed websites, while market share is its percentage of websites with a known CMS.

    Data from W3Techs, Nov. 13, 2026. (WooCommerce and Elementor are not listed in the table above as they’re WordPress plugins and not standalone CMS platforms.).

    *Graphs are separated due to the dominance of the WordPress market share.

    WordPress remains the most widely used CMS. Its usage across all surveyed websites rose from 23.3% in January 2015 to 43.2% in January 2022, before falling to 39.2% today.

    But its long-standing growth curve is now in a downturn. Its CMS market share has fallen by approximately 7.3 percentage points from the January 2022 figure of 65.2%. Since Jan. 1, 2026, it has declined from 60.2% to 57.9%, while all-website usage has dropped from 43.0% to 39.2%.

    It has been revealed that those figures do not show why individual sites changed platforms. For teams using WordPress, plugin compatibility, core updates, and security management remain practical considerations.

    Read more: Should You Still Use WordPress?

    According to recent reports, as the second-most popular standalone CMS in W3Techs’ current listing, Shopify’s market share stands at 7.9%, and it is used by 5.4% of all websites surveyed. Both measures have increased from Jan. 1, 2026, when they stood at 7.0% and 5.0%, respectively.

    Sources indicate that market share is not a performance benchmark. For a separate, historical comparison of technical performance, see our 2025 Core Web Vitals CMS rankings.

    From an SEO and business perspective, Shopify’s growing footprint makes it a platform worth evaluating alongside the features, costs, and technical requirements of an online store.

    Wix now powers 4.2% of websites surveyed and holds 6.2% of the known-CMS market. Its market share has increased from 5.8% at the start of 2026, but its all-website usage remains at 4.2% at the displayed precision.

    Wix has benefited from its positioning beyond a lightweight website builder that consistently invests in branding and platform capabilities, making it a viable contender for mid-market adoption.

    Squarespace’s CMS market share has grown from 0.5% in January 2015 to 3.6% today, with 2.4% of all websites surveyed now using the platform.

    Its growth could be attributed to the increasing demand for low-maintenance, design-forward platforms that are easily accessible to small businesses and individuals.

    Read more: WordPress Vs. Squarespace – Which One Is Better?

    In a recent development, in contrast to all the other top CMS surveyed, Joomla and Drupal have continued to lose CMS market share, now accounting for 1.6% and 0.9%, respectively. At the start of 2026, those figures were 1.9% and 1.1%.

    Once platforms in favor with web developers and amateur coders, this shift likely reflects a broader trend where more user-friendly, SaaS-based platforms capture the attention of small businesses and non-technical users.

    Webflow, which last year looked like a growing contender, now holds at 1.2% of the known-CMS market, unchanged from Jan. 1, 2026. Its usage across all surveyed websites has slipped from 0.9% to 0.8%.

    Sources indicate that between Jan. 1 and Nov. 13, 2026, the proportion of websites using none of W3Techs’ monitored CMS platforms rose from 28.6% to 32.3%, an increase of approximately 3.7 percentage points. During the same period, WordPress usage fell from 43.0% to 39.2% of all surveyed websites.

    Recent findings suggest that that reverses the earlier downward trend in the “no CMS” category. It is not proof that those sites are custom-coded or have abandoned a CMS, as the category means that no monitored CMS was detected.

    Sources indicate that since January 2024, Joomla’s CMS market share has fallen from 2.5% to 1.6%, while Drupal’s has declined from 1.6% to 0.9%. Over the longer period, Joomla has dropped from 8.6% in January 2015 and Drupal from 5.1% in the same month.

    They’ve slipped from the No. 2 and No. 3 spots to No. 5 and No. 10, overtaken by faster-growing platforms like Wix and Squarespace in 2022.

    Joomla, in particular, had strong momentum early on – briefly surpassed WordPress in search interest until around 2008, according to Google Trends – but it hasn’t kept pace with modern platform demands.

    Shopify is the platform with the most interest overtaking WordPress.

    Why did these popular content management systems decline so much?

    It has been revealed that it’s most likely due to the strength of third-party support for WordPress with plugins and themes, making it much more accessible. But the rise of supported themes and plugins for Shopify is starting to gain on WordPress.

    It has been revealed that the growth of website builders, such as Wix and Squarespace, indicates that small businesses want a more straightforward managed solution, and they have started to nibble on market share from the bottom. Although, it does not establish that users moved directly from Joomla or Drupal to those platforms.

    Over the period from November 2025 to November 2026, the CMS market share of:.

    Growth has slowed sharply for Wix and Squarespace, while Shopify’s has accelerated from 4.6% to 16.2% and taken the lead against the others in a reversal from the last reported period (Wix was growing by 32.6%, Squarespace 9.7%, and Shopify by 4.6%).

    It has been revealed that as mentioned above, SaaS web builders don’t require coding knowledge and offer an opportunity for a small business to get a web presence promptly. The rise of Shopify could be attributed to an influx to the platform from WooCommerce, as the WordPress alternative.

    According to recent reports, wordPress is not known as a complicated platform to use, but it does require some coding knowledge and an understanding of how websites are built. On the other hand, a website builder is a much easier route to market, without the need to understand what is happening in the back end.

    Elementor is the most widely used WordPress page builder, installed on 18.2% of all websites with a known CMS and 12.3% of all sites surveyed (not shown below) – more than Wix and Squarespace combined – though it functions as a plugin within WordPress, not a standalone CMS.

    Recent findings suggest that while not a CMS on its own, it is a major part of the WordPress ecosystem. Its figures overlap with WordPress and should not be added to WordPress’s market share or usage.

    W3Techs also compares platforms by overall popularity and traffic rank. The ranking bars measure a platform’s share among sites with a known CMS within each ranking tier, rather than its share of all websites.

    Sources indicate that the WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal comparison above indicates Drupal with a smaller overall footprint but a stronger presence among highly ranked sites. WordPress remains much more widely used overall.

    Wix and Squarespace have lower representation in the top-ranked groups than in the overall known-CMS sample. That is a traffic-ranking distinction, not a direct measure of business size or the quality of the software.

    Elementor gives site owners a visual way to build within WordPress. For businesses comparing drag-and-drop tools, the practical question remains how the builder fits their design, maintenance, and SEO requirements.

    WooCommerce has seen a decline to 11.4% of websites with a known CMS, while Shopify has increased to 7.9%.

    WooCommerce powers 7.7% of all websites surveyed, compared with Shopify’s 5.4%. As a WordPress-based ecommerce platform, it is included within the WordPress ecosystem rather than listed as a separate standalone CMS in the top 10 above.

    W3Techs’ separate ecommerce-system survey uses a different denominator: websites using an ecommerce system that W3Techs monitors. On that measure, WooCommerce has a 47.0% share and Shopify 32.7%. Those figures do not measure sales, revenue, or every online store worldwide.

    In comparison to other ecommerce CMS platforms, WooCommerce is still dominant right now.

    Recent findings suggest that it has more market share than its competitors combined: Shopify (7.9%) + PrestaShop (0.7%) + OpenCart (0.4%). But it is losing ground, and this could be correlated to the decline of WordPress and owners moving to other platforms. It will be interesting to see if Shopify overtakes in the next year.

    The ranking comparison also shows why overall adoption is only part of the picture. Shopify has a stronger presence than WooCommerce in several of the higher-ranked groups, even though WooCommerce has the larger overall share of the known-CMS sample.

    According to recent reports, shopify surged during the pandemic, with market share growing by 52.9% from 2020 to 2021 and then 26.9% from 2021 to 2022, outpacing every other platform. After a dip in 2023, it recovered in 2024 and has reached 7.9% market share this year.

    As the market changes, platform choice affects site architecture, plugin availability, and technical SEO flexibility.

    WordPress continues to lead, but its gradual decline marks a turning point. SaaS competitors such as Shopify, Wix, and Squarespace are steadily gaining traction, offering streamlined platforms that appeal to most businesses.

    If more SMBs are switching to website builders, understanding the limitations and intricacies of these platforms for SEO could be a competitive advantage. CMS adoption determines how efficiently teams can build, secure, and optimize sites at scale.

    The one area I am most interested in is how AI and vibecoding might impact CMS platforms and if there will be a rise in websites without a CMS.

    Shopify now runs on 5.4% of all websites surveyed, not just sites with a CMS. With its increasing footprint, specializing in Shopify SEO could be a strategic move for an SEO professional.

    Wix and Squarespace remain important alternatives, too. Getting fluent in their ecosystems could help you serve businesses with different development and maintenance requirements.

    The reality is that WordPress remains the largest ecosystem in this survey, while other platforms give business leaders and SEO professionals an opportunity to diversify their expertise.

    Understanding the strengths and limitations of various CMS platforms can inform strategic decisions and align with evolving market demands.

    CMS usage and market-share data collected from W3Techs on Nov. 13, 2026. Historical comparisons use the dates stated in the text. Percentages are rounded by the source, so calculated changes are approximate. See the W3Techs methodology page for how the survey is compiled. Google Trends measures search interest separately.

    From latest majors to search traffic, newspapers to impeachment: Have you kept up with this week’s media news?

    Recent findings suggest that it’s been another busy week. Recap it with the second edition of the Nieman Lab News-About-News Quiz, your weekly incentive to keep up with the latest happenings in the world of digital journalism. All questions are based on the week’s Nieman Lab stories or articles elsewhere that we’ve linked to in What We’re Reading. The quiz will appear here through November as a trial run; if people seem to like it, we’ll keep it going in 2027. Good luck!

    What journalism organization announced this week that it was canceling its annual conference and laying off most of its staff?

    Recent findings suggest that “Since we gathered in Chicago for ONA26, many of you have asked when we will be together again,” CEO Niketa Patel wrote. “Unfortunately, it will not be in 2027. ONA has decided to pause our in-person events and will not host a conference in 2027.”.

    For the first time ever, the press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has officially called for the impeachment of a U.S. official. Which one?

    Recent findings suggest that “RSF does not take the question of impeachment lightly. In fact, our organization has never before called for the removal of a US official. But the severity and persistence of Carr’s misconduct as FCC chairman demand an extraordinary response. Congress has a constitutional responsibility to hold him accountable. Restoring the FCC’s independence must be central to that effort.”.

    Emerson College recently unveiled a upcoming degree program aimed at helping students build “a career across a rapidly changing media landscape.” What’s the program’s name?

    “Our fresh Content Creation major prepares students to be a part of the evolving creator economy, teaching them not only how to produce compelling digital content but also how to build a successful entrepreneurial career.”.

    What news organization — after a challenging few years — claims it is now “within striking distance of break-even,” financially?

    Sources indicate that “I’ll be honest,” executive editor Matt Murphy said at a conference. “We had years of losses, and steepening losses. That’s the truth. We’re a private company and don’t share the figures, but it was hundreds and hundreds of millions of dollars. Now we’re within striking distance of break-even, and I expect next year will be our best year in seven years. We’ve done the right-sizing we needed, which was tough.”.

    The Echo-Pioneer — the local newspaper in the town of High Level, Alberta (population 4,000) — has an unusual business model. What is it?

    According to recent reports, town officials signed a two-year “advertising and readership agreement” in 2025. It’s one of the many ways local Canadian news outlets are trying to stay afloat — most notably the federal Local Journalism Initiative.

    Which online publisher’s CEO announced that Google search traffic had “dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week” in October?

    As a result of the search decline, CEO Steve Huffman unveiled Reddit would be shifting to a primarily “logged-in experience.”.

    The Asia-Pacific outlet The Diplomat retracted an interview with a South Korean CEO last week. Why?

    “The author presented themselves as a South Korean freelance journalist and claimed to have interviewed Newtype’s CEO. We now know that the journalist fabricated the interview and may not even be who they claimed to be.”.

    In a recent development, the parliament of an Asian nation is debating requiring tech companies like Google and Meta to pay news outlets when they direct users to their stories. Which nation?

    The proposed law would also require compensating news publishers when AI models are trained on news content.

    Which international news outlet, sensing a political opening, is expanding its reporting team in the United States?

    It has been revealed that “Market research indicated there was room to grow among politically liberal Jews in the United States. Gali Arnon, who became the chief executive of Haaretz Group last year, stated she wanted the newspaper to become in other countries what it is in Israel: an ‘identity brand.’”.

    This photo highlights an early editorial proposal from one of the first important publications on the World Wide Web, a mononymic website that has recently been in the news. What site was it?

    In a recent development, the photo is from Salon co-founder Laura Miller, laying out some early “complications” of the influential web “magazine” which closed last week. “People sometimes tell me about reading Salon avidly in their youth, how it felt like connecting to something exhilarating and cool and a bit crazy in the strange latest expanses of the internet. All I can say is: That’s exactly how it felt to work there.”.

    The most vital stories about journalism and the future of news, delivered to your inbox every afternoon.

    ONA, OpenNews, and others see troubled times ahead, so it's goodbye to "rubber chicken dinners.".

    Industry observers note that the fresh budget would make a local reporting program permanent and extend a 35% tax credit on newsroom salaries. The support makes “a massive, massive difference.".

    The Cornell Daily Sun saw traffic spike by almost 500% in September.

    It has been revealed that RELATED ARTICLESearch traffic has declined so much that some publishers are considering opting out of Google entirelyNeel DhaneshaJuly 22, 2026We’ve now been publishing roundups of local newspaper traffic for a full year, so we can compare this year’s traffic to last year’s. Almost across the board, local newspapers are seeing traffic decline as Google referrals drop. For July, August, and September, traffic to the most-visited sites is lower than at this time last year, according to our Similarweb data.

    RELATED ARTICLEHow did newspapers in places like Harrisburg, Birmingham, and Syracuse become some of America’s most-read online?Joshua BentonJuly 23, 2025A good example is Advance Local’s Harrisburg Patriot-News, PennLive.com. Josh has written about Advance publications punching above their weight in traffic. They still are: Advance outlets like AL.com, Mlive.com, and NJ.com, among others, continued to feature prominently in the top sites by estimated monthly visits in July, August, and September. In August 2026, PennLive’s traffic growth stood out even among Advance peers; it gained 3.6 million visits in August compared to July, a 78% spike. But in total, PennLive saw a little over 8.2 million monthly visits for August 2026 — down from about 12.5 million in August 2025.

    Still, publishers large and small are finding ways to bring more readers to their sites. In August, the Bozeman Daily Chronicle grew its traffic by about 96,000 monthly visits, a 49% jump. Managing editor Jack Reaney attributed the growth to the newspaper launching a newly introduced website Aug. 3 designed for improved functionality, with “fewer, more intentional news categories,” lighter page design for faster load times, and a more modern layout. The Chronicle is one of more than 150 newspapers owned by Adams MultiMedia. The parent company is rolling out the new website design across its newspapers, but Bozeman was the “guinea pig,” Reaney remarked.

    Sources indicate that in Florida, Cape Coral Breeze, a small weekly, saw its traffic spike about 139% in August. The network of local weeklies has tried to adopt a daily, real-time mindset after decades of posting once a week, Breeze Newspapers publisher Ray Eckenrode told me. The August spike was driven by participation in Cape Coral Breeze’s “Best of Cape Coral” contest, where readers vote on favorite local businesses in more than 200 categories. According to the team’s internal count, a little over 150,000 “Best of” votes were cast this year, up from 92,000 last year. The team made an effort this year to “drive traffic to our homepage first to reach the contest voting page to expose some of those casual website customers to our news coverage,” Eckenrode said, and had some success with that strategy.

    According to recent reports, in September, The Cornell Daily Sun gained 1 million visits, almost a 500% jump from August, when it broke the story of the Cornell 7 lawsuit (and published an editorial naming the defendants). Other local news sites in Fresh York also saw meaningful growth in September; traffic to NNY360.com jumped 84%, while the Gannett-owned Democrat and Chronicle gained about 762,000 visits, a 35% jump.

    On the opposite coast, the San-Jose-based Mercury News gained around 690,000 monthly visits in September, a 14% jump. “Our traffic is volatile like everyone else’s, but we had a strong September mainly because a couple of stories performed very well,” said Annika Toernqvist, MediaNews Group’s managing editor for digital for Northern California. Environmental beat reporter Paul Rogers‘ story about a fresh California law that will ban watering artificial turf “performed exceptionally well on Google and Google Discovery”; 62% of traffic to the story came from search. Stories about the local impact of new state laws consistently do well with the outlet’s readers, according to Toernqvist, and this was “a hot topic with a strong headline.” The story was also the top subscription converter in September. Another story by Rogers covering the proposed renaming of Fremont State Park also drove traffic that month; 86% came from search, mostly from Google Discovery.

    Meanwhile, celebrity reporter Martha Ross‘ story about a new book on King Charles’ valet performed well in part thanks to a bump from…the Drudge Report. (“Yes, the Drudge Report still drives traffic,” Toernqvist noted; it accounted for 43% of visits to that story.).

    Google’s Ask Maps Starts Finding Appointments & Calling Businesses via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (675 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Open appointment slots at beauty, pet care, auto and home-repair businesses are starting to show up in Ask Maps, Google Maps’ AI chat.
    • It has been revealed that the feature is part of a set of Ask Maps updates that started rolling out Monday on Android and iOS.
    • Business Profile already has a setting for calls Google makes on behalf of customers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Open appointment slots at beauty, pet care, auto and home-repair businesses are starting to show up in Ask Maps, Google Maps’ AI chat. Google indicates Ask Maps can look for these appointments online and phone the businesses for a customer.

    It has been revealed that the feature is part of a set of Ask Maps updates that started rolling out Monday on Android and iOS. Appointment finding is launching first in the U.S.

    Business Profile already has a setting for calls Google makes on behalf of customers. Google’s post doesn’t say whether Ask Maps calls follow it.

    Google’s post describes appointment finding in Ask Maps this way:.

    “Now, with latest agentic capabilities, you can choose to have Ask Maps find beauty, pet care, auto and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you.”.

    Recent findings suggest that google’s example request is “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me.” Ask Maps then highlights openings at nearby businesses “so it’s easy to decide what to book,” according to the post.

    Google’s demo shows Ask Maps confirming the service, location and preferred time before checking availability.

    According to recent reports, google’s Business Profile help page on automated calls indicates that when customers use Google Search or Maps to connect with a business, Google might call that business on their behalf to complete the request. The requests it lists include booking appointments and confirming the price and availability of services. If a business works with online booking providers, the page says Google may book through the partner or call the business directly.

    Verified businesses manage these calls in Business Profile under More, then Business Profile settings, then Advanced settings. The section labeled “Google automated calls and text messages” has a toggle for “Bookings and inquiries from customers.” A business can also ask a Google caller to stop calling.

    Recent findings suggest that the help page claims these calls are available in every U.S. state except Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana and Nebraska.

    According to recent reports, google has called local businesses for searchers before. In July 2025, I covered the rollout of AI calling in Search, where people searching for a service such as auto repair or a pet groomer can tap “Have AI check pricing” and have Google call several providers nearby. Google’s help page for that feature says the person then gets an email with quotes.

    When it introduced in Search, a Google spokesperson stated the AI picks which businesses to contact based on traditional local search rankings. Google’s Ask Maps post doesn’t say how Ask Maps chooses businesses to check or call.

    At I/O in May, Google remarked people could ask it to call businesses “for select categories like home repair, beauty or pet care.” Three of the four Ask Maps categories match those examples.

    Google’s Ask Maps post notes the chat is starting to expand to 30 countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany and the U.K., bringing it to more than 200 countries and territories. Itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered, while appointment finding starts in the U.S.

    Ask Maps puts openings from nearby businesses in front of a customer in the same conversation where they pick a place to book. For beauty, pet care, auto and home-repair businesses in the U.S., that’s a new place to win an appointment, and Ask Maps can call them to check openings.

    Recent findings suggest that the “Bookings and inquiries from customers” toggle in Business Profile is the control Google documents for calls it makes for customers through Search and Maps. Check where yours is set, and let whoever answers your phone know these calls come from Google on a customer’s behalf.

    It has been revealed that google says more regions are coming soon for Ask Maps’ appointment finding, though the post names none and gives no date. Watch the Business Profile help page for word on whether the “Bookings and inquiries from customers” toggle and the five-state exclusion cover Ask Maps’ calls.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that in a world where many social apps measure their success by time spent online, Places offers a different kind of product built by Raya, a technology organization focused on providing utility. Our apps, Raya and Places, are tools for discovery of and access to exciting people and places globally. We believe that by marrying great software with a membership-based community built around core values of trust, curation, and authenticity, we can provide solutions that offer something different to infinite content and AI-slop. Places’ mission is to help discerning global travelers find their favorite places wherever they go through expert curation and community trust.

    As a Data Scientist on the Places by Raya team you will play a key role that will shape how the Places app uses data to drive business decisions. This hands-on role combines data modeling and reporting with product analysis and experimentation. While the product itself has existed since 2023 the culture is very much like a new start-up with leadership being heavily invested in this product space and this role being the first dedicated Data Scientist to this space and supported by a dedicated Data Engineer.

    Industry observers note that we are seeking an entrepreneurial and driven data scientist to identify opportunities to improve retention and help the team evaluate and act on them. This will be a fun role for someone who wants to build data solutions from the ground up and help shape how the entire team uses insights. This person should be able to articulate best practices, develop fresh analytical frameworks that tie user actions to outcomes, and strike the right balance between analytical rigor and pragmatic business action.

    In a recent development, successful candidates will demonstrate technical skills, product expertise, and business acumen, and be enthusiastic about making a positive impact through timely execution. You are passionate about leveraging the power of data to drive product changes with quality and agility and can demonstrate sound judgment under uncertainty.

    NPR makes fixing its app a key priority in its latest strategic blueprint

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (693 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Niemanlab

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that all the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing.
    • Industry observers note that we have sent a confirmation link to .
    • Over the next two years, NPR will address a longstanding listener plea: improving its app.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that all the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing. Our daily newsletter is a must-read from newsrooms to executive suites.

    We will never sell your address. Prefer a weekly email?

    Nearly there — check your email.

    Industry observers note that we have sent a confirmation link to . Click it and you are on the list. If it has not turned up in a minute or two, it may be in your spam folder.

    Over the next two years, NPR will address a longstanding listener plea: improving its app.

    In a recent development, during a November 12 board of directors meeting, NPR CEO Katherine Maher noted the organization will rebuild its digital offerings to be a “service-first, app-first destination” as part of NPR’s 2027-2029 strategic plan, Current reported on Thursday. One goal of the plan is to reach “five million weekly active people on its platforms by 2029” and “to build a monthly engaged digital audience of 40 million.” According to Current, Maher said that the NPR network — which includes more than 200 member radio stations — currently reaches 39 million weekly listeners across broadcast and digital, but the “total potential addressable audience, weekly consumers of news, information and culture who are open to our work, is roughly 153 million Americans. That is nearly four times our current reach.”.

    According to recent reports, in Apple’s App Store, NPR’s app has a 4.7-star rating and more than 78,000 reviews, of which the majority are positive. But reviewers have quibbles.

    Bryan Moffett, NPR’s senior vice president of transformation, said NPR+, the broadcaster’s subscription program, brought in $8 million in the 2026 fiscal year, up from $5.5 million in 2025. (NPR+ is available with a donation of $8 a month or more, and offers perks like podcasts without ads.) Maher said new investment in the app will help reach younger audiences and shift NPR’s “median audience age from 60-plus toward 40-plus.”.

    “We love radio, but we have been so wildly successful there that we’ve largely exhausted its further financial growth,” Maher told the board. “And as it shrinks, we must invert our revenue engine to ensure sustainability across all of our platforms, including radio, but to build a wider funnel through digital offerings, third-party platforms, and new investments in marketing and communication that will tell our story and share our value with the world.”.

    RELATED ARTICLENPR, the quintessential audio news brand, adapts to a video-first futureSarah ScireSeptember 29, 2026Overhauling the app is just one part of NPR’s strategy to keep up with users’ changing consumption preferences. In September, Sarah Scire reported on the broadcaster leaning into video podcasts with the acquisition of Kevin Roose and Casey Newton’s technology podcast Machine Gods. NPR chief operating officer Ryan Merkley told Current in June that NPR was already working on redesigning the app to better serve member stations and their listeners.

    “Fix the app,” departing public editor Kelly McBride told NPR leaders during the meeting. “It’s not a great experience for the audience and it’s key to moving forward, but you guys seem like you’re on it. So I won’t dwell on that.”.

    #20406. Google Adds Branded & Multimodal Data To Search Console API via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Google Adds Branded & Multimodal Data To Search Console API via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, google has declared that it is adding three features from its Search Console Performance report to the Search Analytics API.
    • According to Google’s blog post announcing this, the API now supports the branded queries filter, multimodal web search data (web multimodal), and filters that are able to track multiple countries or device types within one API call.
    • The blog post explains how all three items have been available in the Performance report since they were first implemented.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, google has declared that it is adding three features from its Search Console Performance report to the Search Analytics API. This means website developers and tool makers can build these features directly into their automated reporting systems.

    According to Google’s blog post announcing this, the API now supports the branded queries filter, multimodal web search data (web multimodal), and filters that are able to track multiple countries or device types within one API call.

    The blog post explains how all three items have been available in the Performance report since they were first implemented. The post then describes the API versions as a solution to “stitching together separate requests or maintaining complex keyword regex lists”.

    Your API results can now include a brandedClassification dimension, which enables you to use either the values BRANDED or NON_BRANDED for filtering or grouping based on branded vs. non-branded searches. According to the API reference documentation, this upcoming dimension provides data only for top-level properties, starting Feb. 21, 2026; however, if a property does not meet the required number of queries and impressions, you will receive an empty table (no rows), the blog post says.

    The API reference documentation also states that the branded classification dimension field accepts only the equals operator, and you cannot apply filters or groupings with it in requests with a query filter applied.

    Google’s earlier announcement highlighted the branded and non-branded options in the Performance report:.

    In March, a Search Console user posted a question noting that their branded breakdown only started at approximately Feb. 21. They then asked if it would be possible to have prior data broken out into two different categories. Google’s John Mueller responded that there is “a point when the data starts being tracked,” as reported by Roger Montti.

    Searches with Google Lens provide multimodal performance metrics when type is set to webMultimodal, as do Circle to Search on an Android device and uploading images to Google Search, according to the reference.

    Industry observers note that after multimodal reporting was enabled by Search Console on Sept. 24, I reported that the API reference did not have a separate multimodal type value listed. The reference, last updated Nov. 16, now lists one.

    Google’s September announcement illustrated the multimodal option in the report’s search-type filter:.

    Sources indicate that google’s September announcement also listed Chrome’s right-click “Search this image” feature, and the Performance report help page includes Chrome image search. The API post and reference don’t mention Chrome.

    The Nov. 16 post states multimodal data “will also be available in BigQuery for properties with an active bulk data export” but doesn’t give a date. As of Nov. 16, the bulk export table reference lists six search types, with no multimodal value yet.

    A brand-newly introduced field, filterLists, enables people to filter results by multiple countries or multiple devices in one request. The examples given in the post are country-based groupings like EMEA, LATAM or DACH.

    The reference limits filterLists to country and device dimensions and matches on exact values only. People cannot use the same dimension (country or device) in filters and in filterLists in the same request.

    On eligible properties, the upcoming feature allows teams using the API to capture a branded/non-branded split in their reporting tools, starting Feb. 21, 2026. For data prior to this date, the API’s split has no ability to break out branded vs. non-branded search traffic.

    It has been revealed that google uses an AI-assisted process to determine which searches are branded or non-branded. According to Google’s November 2025 announcement, “some queries may occasionally be misidentified”. To identify discrepancies, run the API branded/non-branded split alongside a brand regex you have been using and see where they differ.

    As of Nov. 16, the API reference does not indicate if web results include webMultimodal data. Before adding your web and webMultimodal totals together, check how your API web numbers match against the text-based and multimodal numbers in the Performance report.

    As of Nov. 16, neither Google’s post nor the API reference explains how far back webMultimodal data goes. Check the API reference and the bulk export table reference for a BigQuery date, the start date for multimodal history, and any mention of Chrome image search.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • In a recent development, we’re looking for a Software Engineer, AI Tooling Infrastructure to join our AI Tooling team and help build and run the backend services behind Supabase’s AI products.
    • Industry observers note that the AI Tooling team runs its own services in production and carries its own on-call.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    In a recent development, we’re looking for a Software Engineer, AI Tooling Infrastructure to join our AI Tooling team and help build and run the backend services behind Supabase’s AI products. The Supabase MCP server is one example of what the team runs in production, alongside the services that support agent skills and the dashboard assistant. You’ll work closely with the Platform, SRE, Auth, Billing and Edge Functions teams, and with the engineers on the AI Tooling team who build the product surfaces.

    Industry observers note that the AI Tooling team runs its own services in production and carries its own on-call. Traffic from AI clients and agents behaves differently from traffic from people: hundreds of calls a minute, retry loops, and no reading of deprecation warnings. This role makes sure the services they use are reliable, correctly authorized and observable. It is a systems and infrastructure role rather than a product AI role, and it is not an SRE role. You will build and operate these systems, not only advise on them.

    This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments, owns what they ship in production, and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

    Build and operate the production backend services behind Supabase’s AI products, including the MCP server: deployment, scaling, configuration and release.

    Take ownership of how those services are structured, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

    Industry observers note that define, measure and meet reliability targets for the services the team runs. Set SLOs with the SRE team, track error budgets, and use them to decide what to fix first.

    Participate in the AI Tooling team on-call rotation, and be a first responder for incidents in those services. Investigate, fix, coordinate with other teams during incidents, and write the follow-ups and runbooks.

    Work the AI Tooling team support queue alongside on-call, and turn recurring complications into fixes rather than repeated manual answers.

    Own authentication and authorization for AI and agent clients: OAuth apps, scoped tokens, and permissions that make sense for agents as well as humans, including how we change or deprecate a permission without breaking existing integrations.

    Own observability for the services the team runs: metrics, traces, logs, dashboards and alerts, so we find problems before customers do.

    Handle capacity and abuse for agent traffic: rate limits, cost and safety controls, and behavior under load or when a dependency degrades.

    Improve the architecture of the services the team owns as they grow, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

    Work with the Platform team on shared code, review ownership and release process, and with the SRE team on infrastructure, alerting and incident practice.

    Contribute to the code of the AI Tooling team’s tools, such as the MCP server, where it affects reliability and security, in partnership with the engineers who own the product surface.

    Have 5+ years of experience building and running backend services in production, and have carried on-call for them.

    Write strong TypeScript or Go, and are comfortable working in the other.

    Have designed and operated APIs with real consumers: versioning, error handling, rate limiting, and backwards-compatible change.

    Know OAuth, OIDC, JWT and API authorization well enough to debug them in production and to explain where implementations commonly deviate from the spec.

    Have a good understanding of PostgreSQL and relational databases.

    Recent findings suggest that are comfortable with CI/CD, Docker and containerized deployments, and with infrastructure as code. Any tool is fine.

    Can debug across services: follow a slow or failing request through several systems using metrics, traces and logs.

    Communicate clearly in writing, work with a wide range of stakeholders, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving promptly.

    Recent findings suggest that pick your centre of gravity. We expect you to be deep in at least one of these, and to tell us which:.

    APIs and auth: You have designed permission models, token scopes or OAuth flows for third-party or machine clients, and you have migrated them without breaking consumers.

    Operations: You have run production services yourself: carried the pager, written alerts and runbooks, used SLOs or similar to decide what to fix, and made shared systems less risky over time.

    Gateways and distributed systems: You have built or run proxies or gateways, or debugged hard failures across services (retries, partial failures, upstream outages, fail-open vs fail-closed decisions), and you can reason about load and degradation.

    Experience with agent tooling (MCP or similar), or serving traffic from AI agents and LLM clients.

    Experience moving a service out of a larger codebase while keeping existing clients working.

    Experience with Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Logflare or a similar observability stack, and real SLO work.

    Open-source contributions, especially to Node.js, Go, TypeScript or API tooling.

    In a recent development, we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Recent findings suggest that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the organization. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Industry observers note that supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

    Recent findings suggest that once a year, the entire tech giant gathers in a upcoming city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    According to recent reports, we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    It has been revealed that we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If an AI answer mentions your brand but recommends a competitor, what have you actually won?

    • [00:00] Meet Patrick Reinhart [03:19] What Enterprise Brands Are Doing In AI Search [05:16] Why Recommendations Matter More Than Rankings [09:48] The AEO Metrics That Matter [12:49] When AI Gets Your Brand Wrong [18:12] Where SEO And AEO Differ [23:50] Why AI Search Has The C-Suite’s Attention [26:31] How Brands Earn AI Citations [30:25] Where To Invest In Your 2027 AEO Strategy [35:25] Where To Find Patrick Reinhart.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If an AI answer mentions your brand but recommends a competitor, what have you actually won? Patrick Reinhart, VP of Services and Thought Leadership at Conductor, joined me on the SEJ Podcast to discuss what enterprise brands should be trying to achieve with answer engine optimization.

    We talk about the difference between citations and recommendations, how AI can repeat outdated information about your business, and why AEO needs input from SEO, PR, social, and leadership. Reinhart also shares where he’d focus first when planning an AEO strategy for 2027.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that cloudLinux is the maker of Imunify360 — a suite of security products protecting millions of websites across the web hosting industry — and of CloudLinux OS, the operating system behind a large share of the world's shared hosting. To learn more about our firm and products, visit our websites: cloudlinux.com and imunify360.com. Alongside those established product lines we run a small innovation team whose job is to find and prove the next ones.

    We are looking for a Product Owner to lead that team: a small, senior, fully remote squad of engineers that takes upcoming product concepts from idea to a working MVP in customers' hands, then hands proven products to a product line and moves on to the next concept. You will be accountable for the pipeline of ideas, the speed and rigour with which they are tested, and the evidence behind every go / no-go recommendation.

    Industry observers note that this is a hands-on lead role, not pure people management: roughly 50% discovery and leadership (customer conversations, scoping, prioritisation, coaching, reporting to the CPO) and 50% building (prototypes, spikes, design and code review, demo stands). You will not be the team's only builder, but you must be able to build a credible prototype yourself and hold a technical opinion about every part of it.

    According to recent reports, you don't need to arrive as an expert in web hosting or security. If you have taken a product from nothing to its first paying customers before — as a founder, an early engineer, or the lead of an incubation team — and you get deep into unfamiliar technical territory fast, we will teach you the market.

    It has been revealed that the innovation team sits across CloudLinux and Imunify and owns the product concepts that do not yet have a home in an established product line. Ideas come from customer conversations, industry events, telemetry across more than 80,000 servers and the CPO’s strategy; the team’s job is to turn them into something a customer will pay for within a quarter, using AI coding agents throughout.

    Prototyping and technical direction.

    We evaluate engineers partly on how effectively they work with coding agents, and in the innovation team this is the main lever on speed. As the lead you model and coach it: prompt specificity, review quality on agent-generated code, context provision, iteration and error recovery, and end-to-end task completion. Expect to use agents to build prototypes, generate test corpora and draft customer-facing material.

    Provide initial and timely responses to all support cases for a variety of topics, from billing or pre-sales requests to usage optimization or disputes.

    Excellent communication skills and fluency in English.

    Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences.

    Have experience in async or globally distributed teams.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving rapidly.

    Being proficient in SQL is a bonus.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are vital to us.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    According to recent reports, supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    We love games. We play games. And together, we grow games that last.

    We believe in the future and power of the mobile gaming industry and that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to build a life they love through games—from anywhere in the world.

    We believe you know when and where you do your best work. We are fully remote by design and we WFA: Work From Anywhere. We don’t impose hours or limit time off.

    It has been revealed that we are looking for a hands-on Games Recruiter who knows where to find great talent in China's gaming industry and how to engage them.     Industry observers note that focused on impact. You understand the 80/20 rule and focus on activities that matter.

    It has been revealed that performance-driven and growth-oriented. You have an intrinsic will to succeed while unafraid to try, fail, and learn by experimenting with new approaches and testing ideas.

    Cooperative. You help others succeed; you give and receive feedback well.

    Relentlessly curious. You ask questions.

    Humble. You ask for help; you are quick to admit and learn from your mistakes.

    SMART. You work and communicate in ways that are Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Relevant, and Time-bound.

    Own full-cycle recruitment for China market positions (and global when needed) and closing hires for roles in sales, marketing, game production, and beyond.

    Stay up to date on the latest recruitment trends, tools, and best practices.

    Experiment with AI and newly introduced sourcing approaches to improve our hiring quality and efficiency.

    Strong knowledge of the Chinese gaming market (or adjacent technology) talent ecosystem.

    Ability to confidently use BOSS, Maimai, Liepin and more to identify and engage candidates; familiarity with additional China market channels and networks.

    • It has been revealed that we are looking for a data-backed, empathetic Growth Copywriter to own the performance and optimization of our end-to-end messaging ecosystem.
    • It has been revealed that full-Funnel Experimentation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Winona is one of the leading telemedicine companies providing HRT for women in menopause. We’ve built all of our technology in house including an EHR, patient care admin system, patient portal, website, marketing technology etc. Winona has two compounding pharmacies and a team of in house physicians providing world-class care via a fully vertically integrated business model.

    It has been revealed that we are looking for a data-backed, empathetic Growth Copywriter to own the performance and optimization of our end-to-end messaging ecosystem. At Winona, copy isn’t just about sounding nice. It’s a measurable variable in our growth funnel. You will design and execute rapid copy experiments across our paid acquisition, intake flows, and lifecycle retention loops to help women confidently access bioidentical HRT and menopause care.

    It has been revealed that full-Funnel Experimentation. Write copy hypotheses, design rapid A/B tests alongside growth and analytics teams, analyze performance data, and turn winning variations into a scalable messaging playbook.

    Lifecycle Growth & Retention. Write, test, and optimize automated onboarding, activation, adherence, churn-save, and win-back sequences across email, SMS, and push notifications to drive LTV.

    High-Intent Conversion Surfaces. Own the persuasive strategy and microcopy for landing pages, interactive quiz/intake flows, checkouts, and dynamic pricing/offer messaging.

    Paid Acquisition at Scale. Generate volume-driven concepts, hooks, and static/video copy variants for Meta, Google, and YouTube, systematically iterating based on creative testing data.

    Voice of Customer (VoC) Intelligence. Continuously mine product reviews, customer support tickets, intake data, and exit surveys to isolate deep qualitative insights and high-converting customer language.

    AI-Augmented Workflows. Leverage and train Winona’s internal AI copywriting tools to scale production velocity, maintain brand consistency, and build automated variant pipelines without sacrificing quality.

    5+ years of dedicated copywriting experience specializing in direct-response, conversion copywriting, or growth marketing.

    DTC Telehealth, Wellness, or HealthTech experience is highly preferred. You understand how to write about sensitive health topics with clinical authority and deep empathy.

    A portfolio backed by data and results — the exact copy variants you tested, the structural or psychological changes you made, and the quantifiable lift they produced in metrics like CTR, quiz completion, or conversion rates.

    Deep lifecycle marketing mastery: significant experience building and optimizing automated email and SMS flows (onboarding, retention, win-backs), rather than just writing one-off promotional campaigns. You know how to nurture a lead over time.

    Mattel brings Barbie, Hot Wheels to TikTok Shop

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Digiday

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that join us Dec.
    • This story was first published by Digiday sibling Modern Retail.
    • According to recent reports, the tech giant is launching a branded storefront on the platform as it looks to get ahead in live commerce.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that join us Dec. 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit.

    This story was first published by Digiday sibling Modern Retail.

    Mattel is bringing its toy box to TikTok Shop.

    According to recent reports, the tech giant is launching a branded storefront on the platform as it looks to get ahead in live commerce. Mattel’s TikTok Shop store debuts this week with roughly 20 products across Barbie, Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price and Monster High properties. Mattel will soon expand the assortment to include more than 40 products.

    Mina Zandbar, Mattel’s vp of global e-commerce, told Modern Retail that Mattel wants to use TikTok Shop for product discovery, engagement and education, alongside its traditional retail channels. Mattel has a TikTok channel with 124,000 followers — and TikTok customers already discuss its products in videos and in comments — but Mattel hasn’t sold goods directly on the platform before. Zandbar said that, by being on TikTok Shop, Mattel can “be with our community where they’re looking for our brands.”.

    Because TikTok account holders must be at least 13 years old, Mattel’s TikTok Shop strategy is geared toward adults, as opposed to children. “Little kids are not going to purchase products for themselves,” Zandbar said. “It’s [more so about] education for their parents.” Mattel’s selection on TikTok Shop has therefore been curated to include products mentioned in existing TikTok content, such as the Fisher-Price Soothe ‘n Snuggle Otter.

    According to recent reports, some of Mattel’s biggest properties already have TikTok pages with avid followings. Barbie, for instance, has 2.5 million TikTok followers, while Hot Wheels has 1.2 million TikTok followers. With its TikTok Shop store, Mattel can appeal to these various fan bases, while also grouping brands under one umbrella. The Disney Store, which introduced on TikTok Shop this year, likewise operates multiple properties, like “Star Wars” and “Frozen,” as one storefront.

    Because TikTok Shop will serve as an entry point for some shoppers, Mattel is focusing much of its TikTok strategy on product recommendations. The manufacturer will create videos to answer common question like, “Which toys are best for a newborn?” Mattel will also invest in livestreaming and work with content creators who are embedded in the toy community and can speak to the company’s audience.

    In a recent development, still, not everyone visiting Mattel’s TikTok Shop page will have kids of their own. Although Mattel is known for children’s products, it also has “a massive community of adults” collecting items like Hot Wheels and Monster High dolls, Zandbar remarked. Amid what’s been dubbed the “kidulting craze,” Mattel will increasingly use its TikTok Shop presence to appeal to adult collectors.

    Industry observers note that mattel is one of a number of major retail companies joining TikTok Shop ahead of the Black Friday sales rush. This holiday season will be the first winter that significant names like Best Buy, Ulta Beauty and Sephora will sell products on TikTok Shop. Nearly a third of U.S. TikTok consumers expect to buy a gift this Black Friday, per TikTok Shop data.

    Mattel’s TikTok Shop launch also comes on the heels of its upcoming loyalty program called Mattel Rewards. Members can earn points on qualifying purchases and activities and redeem their points for discounts at checkout. The program includes four tiers, with benefits increasing based on annual spend. Already, more than 25% of Mattel’s consumers belong to the program.

    Recent findings suggest that as Mattel sees it, TikTok Shop and a loyalty program serve different, but compatible functions. With a loyalty program, Mattel can more closely communicate with its most avid fans and build relationships with them, Zandbar noted. Mattel can also collect first-party data on everything from someone’s average order value to their location. TikTok Shop, meanwhile, helps with discovery, but it also keeps transactions and data within its own ecosystem. Both, Zandbar said, allow Mattel to “stay as close as you can to your community.”.

    Zandbar acknowledged that the holidays may be a hectic time to launch new marketing channels. But that can also work in Mattel’s favor, she mentioned. “I just believe the busiest time is going to give you massive data to understand what is truly working or not working,” she said. “I want to make sure we are maximizing our learnings during the busiest time of the year.”.

    In a recent development, mattel forecasts it will end its fiscal 2026 year in a strong position. For its third quarter ending in September, Mattel reported net sales of $1.807 billion, up 4% year over year on a reported basis. Mattel’s operating income totaled $476 million, up $96 million. Action figures, building sets, games and Hot Wheels saw gains, while Barbie and Fisher-Price saw declines.

    Mattel also has a new CEO in Roger Lynch, who assumed his position in early November and is focused on driving growth at the 81-year-old tech giant. “My first few weeks leading Mattel have reinforced my belief in the company’s potential,” he stated in an earnings release. “I also see clearly where we must improve. … Our priorities are clear: strengthen our brands and win in toys, drive innovation and creativity, and invest with discipline to drive profitable growth.”.

    Marketers use creator, influencer and tastemaker interchangeably, but the industry still hasn’t settled on what the labels mean.

    A fresh product manager role will explore ad-related monetization, suggesting the platform could make ads a bigger part of its business.

    CEOs have never cared much for holdcos. Enterprise solutions, on the other hand, get a meeting.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that join us Dec.
    • The gradual erosion of the power of local sports through the regional sports network system — brought on largely by cord-cutting that’s seen cable and MVPD penetration drop to well below 40% of all TV homes — has led many sports fans to struggle to find their favorite local baseball, hockey or basketball team.
    • It has been revealed that that confusion, one would think, might lead to depressed ratings and a struggle to secure ad revenue for those respective teams.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that join us Dec. 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit.

    The gradual erosion of the power of local sports through the regional sports network system — brought on largely by cord-cutting that’s seen cable and MVPD penetration drop to well below 40% of all TV homes — has led many sports fans to struggle to find their favorite local baseball, hockey or basketball team.

    It has been revealed that that confusion, one would think, might lead to depressed ratings and a struggle to secure ad revenue for those respective teams. Not so, insists Craig Sloan, CEO of Playfly Sports, a sports rep firm that deals with 83 teams across those three professional sports, and is expanding into selling OOH, experiential and other media around teams and leagues.

    Recent findings suggest that sloan noted the continued strong ad marketplace for sports, which formed the single strongest line of content to be sold in this year’s upfront marketplace. He remarked he also expects streaming to continue to increase its share of sports viewership as linear TV sees its share erode further.

    In a recent development, the bankruptcy of Main Street Sports Group (MSSG) earlier this year forced 20 NBA and NHL teams to change their TV and streaming partners, and eight more changed their streaming home. Throughout, Playfly kept 100% of its rights and is selling local media for all 83 of its teams this season, landing local ad sales deals with several media channels, including TV station groups Sinclair, Scripps, Gray and Nexstar, along with sports streamer DAZN.

    Sloan spoke with Digiday about the health of the marketplace and the impact of streaming on viewership and ad sales.

    The following Q&A has been lightly edited for space and clarity.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s been a slow progression of how people have started engaging. The amount of people that are now watching through streaming for our local games across the country is not insignificant. It is in the mid to high teen [percentages] of total audience for any particular game, and we see a path in the not too distant future where over a third of the audience will come in through streaming. The remainder will be on traditional linear TV. That is all predicated on the idea that traditional linear TV looks the same in three to five years from now, which I would not be betting on.

    Industry observers note that the leagues [NHL, NBA and MLB] are more interested than ever before about consolidating their local rights into a centralized platform. Whether that happens or not — whether the teams will want that or whether fans will have a say in that or not — remains to be seen. It’s all being discussed at the present.

    We have been in discussions with each one of the leagues individually about that potential and what they’re thinking that might be best to happen there. So no firm decisions. The NBA probably is the first decision because they’ve been talking about doing this in a consolidated platform potentially as soon as the 27-28 season, meaning next season.

    The NBA is thinking about creating a platform with potentially one of the streaming partners to consolidate all 30 teams into one platform for their local games. So you would still only get your local game, but you’d go into one environment and you’d pick up your Knicks or whoever. The league hasn’t thought that they would have every team in the product, but they’re still figuring that out.

    If they can get the majority of the teams to opt in, they can go to market with something that a that a very much a streamer would likely bid on, and then they can add other teams in if teams want to eventually opt in.

    In a recent development, the teams might push back and say we want to keep it the way that it is, and they might win. The league might say we’re going to give up on the opportunity. But I think they’re clearly going down a path of exploring this potential option. Because everybody’s end goal is to create an environment where the fans know where the games are, it’s widely distributed so everyone has access to it, and engagement levels remain high, so that the the sport continues to grow.

    We’ve kept the marketplace — advertisers and agencies — focused in on the importance of this space, and to not get caught up in the soap opera and the drama of where are they going to go? At the end of the day, the games will always be on. We’ve been able to still transact in the upfront process, [as well as] scatter, doing sponsorship level deals, [and] highly integrated partnerships — and nothing’s been disrupted thankfully. So we have not had a degradation of our narrative and/or our results.

    In a recent development, we are sitting here on a weighted average because we have every team, so some winners, some losers. Every year, like an annuity, we get to bring out a similar, if not improved, supply. One of the calling cards for us in the marketplace is although the media rights holder might change, the fans are going to show up no matter what.

    In general it’s been an okay marketplace, heavily predicated in the sports world — and probably overall —on football spending: NFL first, college football second, and then everything else in sports has fallen behind that.

    According to recent reports, the scatter marketplace never materialized … In today’s environment, you have to still count quite a bit on a healthy upfront to do well in a in a calendar year. From that perspective, we would still like to see more of a return to scatter. There were certain brands this year that decided to sit out the upfront and remarked that they just like the optionality of coming in in scatter, and that’s just starting to materialize.

    AI certainly is, and we’ve got now this prediction marketplace. Sports betting is sort of settling in, but dependent upon what the leagues will continue to allow in their rulings for for what we can sell, that could be a very healthy category for us between Polymarket, Kalshi and others. Tourism and travel are back on the upswing as are financial services which are up significantly.

    Women’s volleyball is going to explode.

    D+ Research: Marketers express revenue optimism for 2026 holiday season despite economic pressures

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, join us Dec.
    • Industry observers note that this research is based on unique data collected from our proprietary audience of publisher, agency, brand and tech insiders.
    • Recent findings suggest that this is an excerpt from our Digiday+ Research report The 2026 guide to holiday marketing strategies, including A-Frame Brands, Mastercard and Ritual, which examined which commerce channels are dominating marketers’ holiday strategies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, join us Dec. 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit.

    Industry observers note that this research is based on unique data collected from our proprietary audience of publisher, agency, brand and tech insiders. It’s available to Digiday+ members. More from the series →.

    Recent findings suggest that this is an excerpt from our Digiday+ Research report The 2026 guide to holiday marketing strategies, including A-Frame Brands, Mastercard and Ritual, which examined which commerce channels are dominating marketers’ holiday strategies. The report is based on a survey of 90 brand and retailer professionals, as well as individual interviews with marketing executives.

    In Digiday+ Research’s holiday report last year, brands and retailers expressed conservative expectations for their 2025 holiday revenue. This year, however, marketers are more optimistic. The majority of survey respondents (76%) remarked they expect their 2026 holiday revenue to increase 1% to 31% or more in comparison to their 2025 holiday revenue.

    Sources indicate that digiday also asked respondents if they expected their 2026 holiday revenue to decrease in comparison to their 2025 holiday revenue. No respondents (0%) mentioned they expected their holiday revenue this year to decrease by more than 11% in comparison to last year.

    While survey respondents were optimistic about their holiday revenue expectations, some of the marketing executives Digiday spoke with remarked inflation is weighing on their minds.

    “It is getting brutal out there,” said Ari Bloom, founder and CEO of brand incubator A-Frame Brands. “Costs are getting so high, and the economy is soft right now, and probably will get softer as we get into the fall. The cost concern is going to be really hard for a lot of smaller companies to absorb with heavy discounting.”.

    In a recent development, bloom added that the political calendar may play a role in holiday spending as well. “When you’re in an election year, you’ve got a different dynamic because there’s a lot of discussion around inflation,” Bloom remarked. “People will have a sentiment of whether the environment is inflationary, whether things are too expensive or there’s an affordability crisis.”.

    It has been revealed that laura Brodie, chief growth officer at supplement company Ritual, mentioned she too is concerned about consumer confidence but remains optimistic overall. “Even with the state of the economy and consumer sentiment sitting at a pretty low point in history, I’m bullish,” Brodie said. “Spending is resilient. It’s less about what happens in holiday spending growth year over year, which will probably be modest. Where the spend actually gets allocated will be interesting to see.”.

    According to recent reports, brodie said she expects consumers to spend more on experiences this holiday season. “We’re seeing a major cultural shift towards nostalgia, being intentional and spending time with family,” she said. “I anticipate people will gravitate towards gifts as experiences or things that feel personal rather than mass purchased. That includes brands that have a distinct point of view, or are mission driven or founder-led. Especially in health and wellness, brands that really speak to a consumer will have a strong opportunity to win.”.

    It has been revealed that while survey respondents expressed optimistic revenue expectations for the 2026 holiday season, the majority of brands and retailers said they don’t have intends to offer deeper holiday discounts this year compared to last year. Eighty-one percent of brand and retailer pros said that they expect their 2026 holiday discounts to be about the same as their 2025 discounts.

    Instead of offering deeper discounts, some brands and retailers are turning to other promotional strategies like bundling products or adding a gift with purchase to entice customers. A-Frame’s Bloom said that economic pressures, including higher transportation and fuel costs, present an additional challenge for the 2026 holiday season.

    “This year will be more sensitive than last year because the economic situation is more difficult and prices are higher,” he mentioned. “We’ve been talking a lot about bundling versus discounting because holiday is a time when people will buy multiples. They might buy the same gift for three different people, and they may buy it for themselves to try on top of it.”.

    Sources indicate that bloom added that offering a gift with a purchase can encourage holiday shoppers to become repeat buyers. “We recommend products, even if it’s trial sizing, that are able to be thrown in a bag,” Bloom stated. “It is a really good way to get people who are buying a gift to keep something for themselves as part of the transaction. There’s ways for brands to think about getting more value out to the customer.”.

    Ritual’s Brodie said offering perks to existing customers during the holiday season encourages brand loyalty and can temper the expense of new customer acquisition. “Offering exclusivity to existing customers and to pull people back with something that feels unique, a compelling gift with purchase or seasonal drop. … The cost of acquisition is high during holiday, so being able to tap an existing audience can be cost-effective.”.

    She explained that Ritual has also partnered with other wellness brands to cross-promote products and provide a gift with purchase during the holidays. “Brands that are in similar sizes can come together and create something that feels compelling that can benefit both brands,” Brodie mentioned. “We’ve partnered with like-minded brands like [skincare brand] Osea and swapped gift with purchases.”.

    Sources indicate that susan Grossman, evp of consumer acquisition and engagement services at Mastercard said in an email that she expects brands to invest in rewards, exclusive access and experiences that extend beyond the holidays this year. “The more sustainable approach is to think about value more broadly. That could be a personalized offer, exclusive access, relevant recommendations, a seamless experience, or an incentive timed to the right moment,” Grossman said.

    “But to do that, you need better signals and smart personalization,” she added. “When brands understand intent, they can be more precise with when, where, and how they use incentives. Instead of blanket discounting, they can create value for the consumers who need an extra nudge while continuing to build long-term loyalty with those who already have an affinity for the brand.”.

    Marketers use creator, influencer and tastemaker interchangeably, but the industry still hasn’t settled on what the labels mean.
